job.title: Chief Experience Officer (CXO) - Bendigo Kangan Institute
job.description:
Chief Experience Officer (CXO)


  • Lead student and customer experience, brand, marketing and service excellence
  • Enterprise-wide executive role with a major education and skills provider
  • Reporting to an inspiring CEO with a supportive and ambitious Board

 


About Bendigo Kangan Institute


Bendigo Kangan Institute (BKI) is a Victorian Government entity and an integrated skills provider that brings together education, assessment and learning. BKI's 150-year history informs its future as a modern, agile organisation delivering future-ready skills, training and assessment solutions, as well as lifelong learning opportunities. The Institute works in close partnership with industry, educators, government and communities to deliver life-changing education and skills assessment. These partnerships provide deep insights that inform education and skills frameworks, teaching, migration and policy, strengthening the broader sector.


BKI comprises four brands: Bendigo TAFE, Kangan Institute, VETASSESS and eWorks, connecting people and industries with the transformative power of education and careers. The Institute transforms lives, strengthens communities, empowers workforces and supports industries to grow and thrive.


BKI has expanded its TAFE offering in Victoria's north-west and will continue to grow its impact sustainably across the state, nationally and internationally. BKI is one of Victoria's largest TAFE providers, with campuses stretching from Docklands to Echuca, including a Tech School at Broadmeadows.

 

About the Chief Experience Officer (CXO) Role


Reporting to the Chief Executive Officer and forming part of BKI's Executive Team, the Chief Experience Officer will shape and lead the organisations customer, student and stakeholder experience, supporting organisational growth, student success, retention and long-term engagement.


The role leads a diverse Customer Experience Portfolio encompassing brand and marketing, customer service, enrolments, VETDSS, registrar services, student wellbeing, counselling, child safety, process improvement and Artificial Intelligence.


The successful candidate will establish a cohesive, whole-of-Institute approach to customer and student experience, embedding an enterprise service excellence framework and strengthening consistency, accountability and performance across customer-facing functions.


A key focus will be leading high-performing multidisciplinary teams, improving operational effectiveness and strengthening collaboration across services, systems and campuses. The role will also oversee brand positioning, customer acquisition, service performance and continuous improvement, ensuring BKI's brand promise is reflected in the experiences of customers, students and stakeholders.


The CXO will provide executive leadership and oversight of responsible AI adoption through the Chief AI Officer, championing innovation that improves accessibility, personalisation, service delivery and organisational efficiency.


As a member of the Executive Team, the role will contribute to effective governance, risk management, organisational performance and long-term sustainability.

 

About You


You will be an accomplished executive with proven experience leading complex customer / student experience, brand, marketing and customer-facing service portfolios within large, multi-site or service-based organisations.


You will bring extensive expertise in customer and student experience design, service models, brand strategy, market positioning and high-volume service operations, together with a demonstrated ability to lead organisation-wide transformation and continuous improvement.


Your commercial acumen will be complemented by the ability to use customer insights, performance data and market intelligence to shape priorities, allocate resources and deliver measurable outcomes.


You will also demonstrate an understanding of emerging technologies and responsible AI adoption, alongside strong governance, risk management and regulatory compliance capabilities.


An influential and collaborative leader, you will have a track record of building inclusive, high-performing multidisciplinary teams, aligning stakeholders across organisational boundaries and fostering accountability and service excellence.


Importantly, you will bring the judgement, adaptability and enterprise leadership required to navigate complexity, lead change and deliver connected, high-quality experiences across a diverse organisation. Experience within the education sector is highly desirable.

job.title: Chief Information Officer - Workplace Injury Commission
job.description:
Chief Information Officer (CIO)


  • Shape technology strategy, investment and transformation
  • Executive role leading technology, digital, cyber and data capability
  • Be part of an organisation making a difference to Victorian workers

 


About WIC


The Workplace Injury Commission (WIC) is a Victorian Government statutory authority providing independent dispute resolution services for Victoria’s workers compensation scheme.


WIC helps resolve disputes between injured workers, employers, WorkCover agents and self-insurers through conciliation and binding arbitration. Operating independently and at no cost to injured workers, WIC plays an important role in supporting fair, accessible and effective resolution of workers compensation disputes.


Purpose-driven and values-based, WIC’s vision is to be the leading dispute resolution authority in Australia, delivering outstanding service to participants while remaining faithful to the legislative basis that enables its work.



About the Chief Information Officer Role


Reporting to the Chief Executive Officer, this newly created executive role will be WIC’s first dedicated CIO. As a member of the Executive Leadership Team, the CIO will provide both enterprise leadership and strategic and operational direction across WIC’s technology and data portfolio.


The role creates, for the first time, a single permanent executive accountability for technology, digital delivery, cyber security and enterprise data. The role will lead the implementation of WIC’s IT Operating Model, bringing together existing technology functions while building the internal capability, governance and disciplines required for the future.


With WIC’s technology and data capability at an early stage of maturity, the CIO will shape the technology vision, IT strategy and enterprise architecture; establish contemporary service management and cyber security practices; strengthen enterprise data and analytics capability; and oversee technology investment, vendors and delivery.


The CIO will also provide technology leadership and assurance across major platform initiatives, including WIC’s case management system and Microsoft Platform Project, while ensuring technology decisions support WIC’s statutory responsibilities, strategic priorities and evolving service needs.


As one of WIC’s six executives, the CIO will share accountability for enterprise strategy, performance and culture. The role will build and empower a capable senior leadership tier, lead organisational change and establish a sustainable technology function that enables WIC’s continued growth and service delivery.



About You


You are an accomplished senior technology leader with experience operating at, or immediately below, executive level and accountability across both technology operations and transformation.


You bring demonstrated experience building or significantly maturing a technology or data function, including operating model design, organisational structure, sourcing strategy, capability development and the establishment of contemporary technology disciplines. You will have led enterprise platform implementation through delivery, go-live and stabilisation, together with significant technology investment, vendor and commercial management.


You bring strong knowledge across enterprise architecture, cloud platforms, IT service management, cyber security, technology risk, data and analytics, with the judgement to set strategic direction, test advice and translate complex technology matters for executive and Board audiences.


You are an enterprise-minded, values-driven leader who can operate effectively within a regulated and accountability-intensive environment. You bring the ability to build capable teams, empower leaders, navigate complexity and establish trusted relationships across government, Boards, executives, technology partners and other stakeholders.


Tertiary qualifications in information technology, engineering or a closely related discipline are required, with equivalent depth of professional experience also considered. Public sector experience is valued but not mandatory; experience within a statutory authority, tribunal, commission, court or similarly regulated environment will be highly regarded.

job.title: Director of Policy and Advocacy - auDA
job.description:
Director, Policy & Advocacy - auDA


  • Lead policy development and advocacy shaping Australia's internet future in a global context
  • Influence government regulation and facilitate multi-stakeholder policy outcomes
  • Strategic leadership opportunity with a nationally significant, purpose-driven organisation

 


About auDA


.au Domain Administration Limited (auDA) is the administrator of Australia's .au domain name system (DNS), a critical component of the nation's communications infrastructure relied upon by internet users in Australia and internationally.


As a not-for-profit, community-based organisation endorsed by the Australian Government, auDA plays an important role in ensuring the secure, stable and reliable operation of .au while championing an open, free, secure and interoperable internet for the benefit of all Australians.


auDA's purpose is to connect Australians to an open internet with trust and confidence. Its responsibilities extend beyond domain administration to developing transparent and responsive .au policies, supporting multi-stakeholder internet governance and contributing to national and international policy discussions.

Guided by its 2026–30 Strategy, auDA is strengthening its capability across four strategic pillars — Trust, Innovation, Impact and Capability — to respond to an increasingly complex digital, technological and geopolitical environment.

 


About the Director, Policy & Advocacy Role


Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer, the Director, Policy & Advocacy is a senior leadership opportunity responsible for shaping auDA's internet policy development, advocacy and advisory based in internet governance principles across domestic, regional and international environments.


The appointment comes at an important time as auDA evolves its organisational structure and repositions its policy and advocacy capability. With the Internet Governance function positioned as a core function within Operations, the Director will play a central role in establishing clear policy priorities, strengthening engagement with industry, community and government, and developing a high-performing policy team.


A particular focus will be advancing auDA's influence on Australian legislative and regulatory developments affecting the digital economy. This includes emerging issues relating to cybersecurity, privacy, online safety and digital duty of care, scams prevention, artificial intelligence and the security of critical infrastructure.

The Director will lead multi-stakeholder policy development processes relating to the .au licensing framework and broader internet policy matters, ensuring that auDA's positions are evidence-based, practical and responsive to the needs of Australian internet users.


The role will also represent auDA contributing to global internet governance processes through various forums to develop and influence on auDA’s policy positions.

Working closely with the Chief Operating Officer, Executive Leadership Team and Board, the Director will provide high-quality advice on emerging legislative and policy issues, establish productive relationships across community, government, industry and technical communities, and lead the development of auDA's policy and advocacy capability.



About You


You are an accomplished policy and advocacy leader with demonstrated experience analysing complex legislative and regulatory issues, developing evidence-based policy positions and influencing meaningful policy outcomes.


You bring substantial experience leading policy development processes involving diverse stakeholders, balancing competing perspectives and translating complex technical, regulatory or legislative matters into clear and practical advice for senior decision-makers.


Importantly, you have a demonstrated ability to work with industry and advocate for changes to national legislation and influence government policy development. You understand how to engage effectively with policymakers, regulators, industry representatives and other stakeholders to build consensus and achieve outcomes.


You are a confident and credible communicator, capable of preparing high-quality policy submissions, strategic briefings and recommendations for executives, Boards and government stakeholders. Your approach combines intellectual rigour, sound judgement and an appreciation of the practical implications of policy decisions.


As a leader, you are collaborative, curious and outcomes-focused, with experience building capability, developing teams and fostering a culture of accountability and continuous improvement. You are comfortable navigating complex stakeholder environments and engaging constructively with differing perspectives.

Experience in internet technology, digital regulation or critical infrastructure would be highly regarded, however, specialist internet governance expertise is not essential. Candidates with strong transferable policy development and legislative advocacy experience, together with the ability to work effectively with technical subject matter experts, are encouraged to apply.


Experience influencing international policy would also be advantageous.


Relevant tertiary qualifications in public policy, law, political science, international relations, technology or a related discipline are desirable.
